note: Muscle MRI in childhood-onset SNUPN-related LGMD shows selective paravertebral, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius involvement despite primarily proximal clinical presentations.

evidence.text: In five patients presenting with proximal weakness starting in childhood, muscle MRI revealed predominant impairment of the paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found. Muscle biopsy showed myofibrillar-like features consisting of myotilin deposits and Z-disc disorganization. MRI showed predominant impairment of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

evidence.text: Two siblings presenting with adult-onset proximo-distal and axial weakness also demonstrated involvement of the paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius, and gracilis muscles on muscle MRI.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement. One patient presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy. Muscle MRI identified involvement in the paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius and gracilis muscles.
